- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot in the short term.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 1–3% in bullish sentiment periods, underperform in bearish sentiment.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — sentiment history should be weighted more heavily than price history for correction.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing to avoid erratic swings.
